quotes.text: Under fire when this magazine is emptied you shout for “ammo” but perhaps No. 2, the ammo carrier, is lying in the rear with a bullet through his napper. Then it's “napoo-fini” (Tommy's French) for Mr. Lewis.
quotes.reference: 1917, Arthur Guy Empey, “Lewis Gun”, in Over the Top, G. P. Putnam's, page 297:

quotes.text: We walked onto the racecourse like a pair of Wyatt Earps, cashed up and plenty of ammo and we walked off like a pair of Elmer Fudds, out of `buwwets'.
quotes.reference: 1995, Paul Vautin, Turn It Up!, Sydney: Pan Macmillan Australia, page 110:

quotes.text: As with handguns and rifles, some ammos are more accurate than others.
quotes.reference: 2011, Mark Brannon, Tom Hanrahan, Shooting Sporting Clays, page 39:

senses.definition: (slang, games, gambling, uncommon) Chips or money, usually at a casino.
(transitive, informal) To load up on ammunition.

quotes.text: "Harry and Hassan are getting the car re-ammoed; they dropped me off here.
